name: Property Management Companies
h1: AI Phone Agent for Property Management: Repairs and Leasing
metaDescription: Calldesk handles property management calls: maintenance requests, emergency routing, leasing inquiries and rent questions across many buildings.
intro: Property managers answer for dozens or hundreds of doors with a small office. The phone mixes tenants with a leaking ceiling, prospective renters asking if a unit is still open, owners wondering about a statement, and vendors confirming an access time. The pressure comes in waves: the first few days of the month bring rent and late-fee questions, a cold snap brings burst pipes and no-heat calls, and evenings and weekends are when tenants notice what is broken but the office is closed. An after-hours answering service often just takes a name and number, and the real urgency of a flooding unit is lost in a pile of messages. A Calldesk agent can answer as the company's AI assistant, find out which property and unit, separate an emergency such as flooding, gas smell or no heat in winter from a routine fix, send emergencies to the on-call technician by transfer, and log routine requests with the details a maintenance coordinator needs. Leasing calls get availability and showing times from the knowledge base. Outbound batch calls can confirm access windows, with unit and time passed per contact.
callTypes: Tenants reporting a leak, no heat, a broken lock or an appliance failure
Emergency calls after hours that must reach the on-call technician
Prospective renters asking about available units, deposits and pet rules
Rent due date, payment portal and late-fee questions around the first of the month
Vendors and contractors confirming access windows to a unit
Owners asking about a statement, vacancy or a repair authorization

sampleCallFlow.speaker: agent
sampleCallFlow.text: Property management office, this is the company's AI assistant. Is this about a repair, a rental, or something else?

sampleCallFlow.speaker: caller
sampleCallFlow.text: There's water coming through my bathroom ceiling.

sampleCallFlow.speaker: agent
sampleCallFlow.text: I'm sorry, that sounds stressful. Is the water coming down right now, and is it near any light fixtures or outlets?

sampleCallFlow.speaker: caller
sampleCallFlow.text: It's dripping steadily and the light is right there.

sampleCallFlow.speaker: agent
sampleCallFlow.text: Please stay away from that fixture and don't switch it on. What's your name, the building address and your unit number?

sampleCallFlow.speaker: agent
sampleCallFlow.text: Thank you, Lena. I'm treating this as an emergency and connecting you to the on-call maintenance technician now. If they can't answer, I'll take a message flagged urgent.

sampleCallFlow.speaker: agent
sampleCallFlow.text: Transferring you. I'll send your name, unit and the description with the call.

setupSteps: Create an agent from the receptionist template and list the properties you manage in its knowledge base with addresses and what each building offers.
Write an emergency definition with your maintenance lead: flooding, gas smell, no heat in cold weather, fire or electrical hazard, then add a transfer to the on-call number for those.
Add extraction fields for property address, unit, tenant name, callback number and a description of the problem.
Add a leasing branch that answers from the knowledge base about available units and books tour slots on a connected calendar.
Test with emergency and routine scenarios, publish, forward the main line, and use webhooks to push requests into your maintenance system.

featuresUsed.howItHelps: Moves true emergencies to the on-call technician during nights and weekends instead of leaving a message in a queue.
Captures building, unit and a description of the issue so a coordinator can create a work order without calling back.
Answers leasing and policy questions, such as pet rules or how to pay rent, for each property you list.
Books tour times for prospective renters on a connected calendar.
Calls tenants to confirm a maintenance access window, with unit number and time passed in as variables.

considerations: Landlord-tenant law governs entry notices, habitability and how maintenance requests must be handled in your area. The agent logs requests; it does not decide what the law requires of you, so confirm with counsel.
Fair housing rules apply to leasing calls. Keep screening questions to criteria applied equally to every applicant and have your compliance resource review the script.
Collection or late-rent outbound calls can fall under debt collection and telemarketing rules. Check with counsel before using automated calls for anything about money owed.
Tenants may share personal information on calls. Decide what the agent may collect and how long you keep transcripts, under the privacy rules that apply to you.

faq.q: How does it tell an emergency from a routine repair?
faq.a: You define the list, such as active flooding, gas odor or no heat in freezing weather. The agent follows your definition and transfers; for borderline cases, set it to err toward the on-call line.

Treat rent payment as something your existing portal handles. The agent can explain how to pay and send tenants to the portal. Calldesk has a payment step on some carrier setups, but verify it against your needs before relying on it for rent.

faq.q: What if I manage buildings in several cities?
faq.a: Put each property's details in the knowledge base and have the agent ask for the address first. You can also give each portfolio its own number and agent.
Many languages are supported on the Standard and Pro voices, while Lite speaks English. Decide per agent which language it should speak.

faq.q: Does it create tickets in my property software?
faq.a: It can send a webhook for each completed call with the extracted fields. Turning that into a work order in your system takes an automation or integration you set up.
